id_syntax.recommended_literal: table:⟨key⟩        (U+27E8 LEFT / U+27E9 RIGHT ANGLE BRACKET)
id_syntax.why: Every minted key is a 26-char Crockford-base32 ULID, or a composite that starts with one, so it BEGINS WITH A DIGIT and is not a safe bare identifier in SurrealQL.
evidence: The codebase NEVER spells a ULID id into SQL text: ids are bound as surrealdb::types::RecordId parameters, e.g. db/enrollment.rs:96 'CREATE $id CONTENT $row'.
type::record(...) is used whenever the key is computed inside a query: db/badge.rs:122, db/class_pump.rs:436, db/course.rs:312, migration_sql.rs:996/1167/1265/1269.

Literal table:key appears ONLY for known-safe keys: migration_mark:board_roster (migration_sql.rs:1354), settings:school (db/chatbot_thread.rs:123), and in unit tests with hand-written keys like user:t.

Backticks are used in this codebase for DATABASE NAMES only (tenant.rs:109-111), never for record ids - the comment there explains that an unquoted 2024school parses as a duration and 12345 as a number in SurrealDB 3.2.
id_syntax.unverified: Whether SurrealDB 3.2 happens to accept a bare digit-leading alphanumeric record id was not executed. Always wrap.

ulid_time_consistency.derivable: A ULID's first 10 characters encode its mint time in ms (Crockford base32). Nothing in the code DERIVES time from an id.
ulid_time_consistency.but: Several listings ORDER BY id and document that as 'newest first' (domain/monotonic_id.rs header, class_member.rs:44, class_course.rs:55).
ulid_time_consistency.seed_rule: Generate each row's ULID FROM its own created_at / *_at millisecond value, so id order and time order agree. Otherwise every 'newest first' list in the UI is scrambled.

pitfalls.what: A required array field with DEFAULT [] on a SCHEMAFULL row. DEFAULT fires on CREATE only. Any later whole-row write (UPDATE ... CONTENT) that omits the key coerces it to NONE and the write FAILS, permanently. That is why settings.meal_slots / dietary_tags are option<> with NO DEFAULT, and why class_blueprint.courses carries no DEFAULT.
pitfalls.seed_rule: Always write every array field EXPLICITLY. Never rely on DEFAULT []. The three that still carry DEFAULT [] are course.teachers, menu_dish.tags, dietary_profile.tags - write them anyway.

pitfalls.where: meal_ledger (migration_sql.rs:846-856), payment_ledger (migration_sql.rs:894-903), plus READONLY columns on chatbot_thread/chatbot_message/homework*/menu*/meal_*/fee_plan*
pitfalls.what: READONLY is per-FIELD, not per-table. A CREATE / INSERT that sets the field for the FIRST time is allowed; any later UPDATE of it is rejected.
pitfalls.seed_rule: meal_ledger and payment_ledger rows CAN be inserted - just get every value right the first time and never UPDATE them afterwards. Same for menu.date/slot, homework.course/created_by/created_at, meal_booking.menu/student/booked_by/created_at, fee_plan_assignment.*, bank_question.created_at, homework_file.file/created_at.

pitfalls.what: An undefined key is SILENTLY STRIPPED on write (it is not an error) - except that SurrealDB rejects a write to a row that still holds a column whose definition was removed. rag_output.payload is the only FLEXIBLE object (migration_sql.rs:211).
pitfalls.seed_rule: A typo in a field name loses the value with no error. Verify every field name against schema.json character by character.

pitfalls.what: Statements inside ONE query batch see the schema as it stood when the batch STARTED. A DEFINE FIELD next to an UPDATE writing that field silently strips the value. This is why MIGRATION_BATCHES is three separate queries.
pitfalls.seed_rule: Run the seed as a query SEPARATE from any schema work, i.e. after migrate() has fully finished.

pitfalls.what: There is NOT A SINGLE DEFINE FIELD ... VALUE or ... ASSERT in the schema (verified by grep). Every enum is enforced only by Rust newtypes.
pitfalls.seed_rule: The database will happily accept an invalid enum string. Nothing writes over your value either. But the API will 500 on deserialization when a Rust newtype cannot parse it back - so the enum lists in this document are HARD requirements even though the DB does not enforce them.

pitfalls.what: record<x> is a TYPE check only - SurrealDB verifies the value is a record pointer into table x, NOT that the target row exists. There is no REFERENCE / ON DELETE clause anywhere. A dangling link is accepted silently and then breaks reads at the application layer (e.g. the on-time backfill's traversal yields no value).
pitfalls.seed_rule: Insert strictly in the topological load_order. (partially unverified: exact SurrealDB 3.2 coercion behaviour for a non-existent target was not executed - but no REFERENCE clause exists, so nothing can enforce it.)

pitfalls.what: UNIQUE indexes that a naive generator will collide on: user_username; session_token; menu_date_slot (date+slot); dietary_profile_student; attendance_event_user; registration_event_user; class_member_class_user; class_course_class_course; enrollment_course_user; parent_link_parent_student; session_attendance_session_user; meal_attendance_menu_student; exam_attempt_exam_user_seq; exam_answer_question_user_seq; exam_result_exam_user_seq; school_slug + builder_username + builder_session_token (control db).
pitfalls.seed_rule: Most of these are ALREADY implied by the composite record id, so a duplicate id and a duplicate index entry are the same bug. user_username and session_token are the two that are NOT implied by the id - guard those separately.

pitfalls.what: Every counter is the AUTHORITY, not a cache (db/cap.rs:1-31). A course whose enrollment_count is wrong denies real students a place and can never be deleted ((enrollment_count ?? 0) = 0 guard).
pitfalls.seed_rule: Write every counter consistently, or omit it (absent reads as zero) only where the backfill will recompute it. Only course.enrollment_count and board.total_stroke_count are recomputed on every boot. term.class_count, class_group.*_count, course_note.file_count, user.board_count, user.marks_given_total and the other staff/student badge tallies have NO backfill and will stay wrong forever.

pitfalls.what: The five student badge counters are seeded ONCE per volume under migration_mark:profile_counters, and the first line of that block is UPDATE user SET homework_submitted_total = 0, homework_on_time_total = 0, exam_sat_total = 0, pomodoro_finished_total = 0, pomodoro_focus_ms_total = 0 - a full reset.
pitfalls.seed_rule: If you seed BEFORE the first boot, migrate() will recompute those five from your rows (good). If you seed AFTER the mark is written, your values stand as written and nothing checks them. Prefer: create the school (which runs migrate), then seed, and set all counters yourself.

pitfalls.what: Every minted key is a ULID or starts with one, so it BEGINS WITH A DIGIT. The codebase never spells an id into SQL text - it binds a RecordId - so the escaping question is new to a seed file. The only literal ids in the repo are safe ones (migration_mark:board_roster, settings:school).
pitfalls.seed_rule: Write user:\u27e801J...\u27e9 (angle brackets), user:`01J...` (backticks), or type::record('user','01J...'). Never bare user:01J....

pitfalls.what: In SurrealQL, n ?? 0 < $cap parses as n ?? (0 < $cap), which is truthy for every row. Always (n ?? 0) < $cap.
pitfalls.seed_rule: Relevant only if the seed script writes its own guarded UPDATEs.

pitfalls.what: These two int columns are NOT unix ms. They are chrono num_days_from_ce() - days from the Common Era epoch, where 1970-01-01 = 719163 (domain/timestamp.rs:88-97, test at :145).
pitfalls.seed_rule: day_number = floor(unix_ms / 86400000) + 719163

pitfalls.what: An IN-PROGRESS work entry or pomodoro stint lives at the FIXED id open_<user ULID>; closing it writes a fresh ULID-keyed row. A second open row for one user is impossible by construction.
pitfalls.seed_rule: Never give a user two rows whose id is open_<their ulid>, and never use a ULID id for a row with finished_at = NONE / check_out = NONE.

pitfalls.what: For exam_attempt / exam_answer / exam_result / answer_image, the FIRST sitting's id is the bare {scope}_{user} with NO _1 suffix, while the seq COLUMN is still 1.
pitfalls.seed_rule: Never write ..._1 as an id. seq=1 -> bare key; seq=2 -> key_2.

pitfalls.what: There is no hardcoded argon2 hash anywhere. Every in-repo SQL user insert uses the placeholder 'x', which can never verify.
pitfalls.seed_rule: Generate a real $argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$... hash for every account that must be able to log in. One shared hash for 250 students is fine and fast.

pitfalls.what: School creation does NOT write a settings row. An absent settings:school row reads as the built-in defaults everywhere.
pitfalls.seed_rule: Seed settings:school ONLY if you need a non-default vocabulary. If you do, write EVERY required field (exam_kinds, exam_kinds.*.name, exam_kinds.*.weight, attendance_statuses, grade_bands) - they are non-option and a missing one fails the write.

pitfalls.what: kind_ref:<exam kind> and slot_ref:<meal slot> rows are created lazily by the first exam_result / menu. They ARE seeded by the backfill on boot - but only once, guarded by count = NONE.
pitfalls.seed_rule: Either seed them yourself (count = the matching row count) or let the boot backfill do it. Do not do both with different numbers.

pitfalls.what: event.audience.users was REMOVED. Writing it will be silently stripped (SCHEMAFULL) and the row will read as a broken audience.
pitfalls.seed_rule: Use {kind:'registration'} + registration rows instead.

pitfalls.what: exam_question.subject is a REQUIRED record<subject>. The boot backfill DELETES every exam_question with subject = NONE (and its answers first).
pitfalls.seed_rule: Every exam_question must name a real subject, and that subject's course should be the exam's course.

pitfalls.what: DEFAULT_AUTH_RATE_LIMIT = 10/min/IP and DEFAULT_API_RATE_LIMIT = 300/min/IP. A 250-student seed driven over HTTP will 429.
pitfalls.seed_rule: Prefer direct SurrealQL over the API for bulk seeding, or raise the env knobs.
